new_candidates.body:
## Where

`docs/simulators/isaac-sim.md` (last changed in 84e00a1, 2025-09-15; also rendered at docs.openmind.com).

## What looks off

1. **Virtual environment name mismatch.** Step 4 creates the Isaac Sim environment as `env_isaacsim`:

   ```bash
   uv venv --python 3.11 --seed env_isaacsim
   source env_isaacsim/bin/activate
   ```

   but the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` example a few lines below points at `env_isaaclab`:

   ```bash
   export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:PATH_TO_VENV/env_isaaclab/lib/python3.11/site-packages/isaacsim/exts/isaacsim.ros2.bridge/humble/lib
   ```

   The note right after it says "We use `env_isaacsim` (Python 3.11) for Isaac Sim", so I believe `env_isaaclab` is a leftover and should read `env_isaacsim`. As written, a reader who copies the line gets a path that does not exist, and the ROS 2 bridge libraries are not found.

2. **"Update your agent name depending on robot type" does not say which name to use.** The launch example is

   ```bash
   CONFIG=unitree_go2_autonomy USE_SIM=true make dev
   ```

   followed by the note, but the G1 counterpart is not given. Listing the config name for G1 next to the Go2 one (or linking to the config directory) would make the step reproducible for G1 users.

## Proposed fix

- Replace `env_isaaclab` with `env_isaacsim` in the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` line.
- Add the G1 config name to the note (e.g. "for G1 use `CONFIG=<name>`"), or a short table Go2 / G1 → CONFIG.

Happy to open a small docs PR for (1) right away, and for (2) once you confirm the G1 config name. Opening this issue first per CONTRIBUTING.md.
new_candidates.title: docs(isaac-sim): LD_LIBRARY_PATH uses env_isaaclab while the venv is created as env_isaacsim; G1 CONFIG name missing

new_candidates.body:
`calcManipulability(J).m.volume` returns exactly 0 for any Jacobian whose smallest singular value is below about 1e-3. `measure` and `condition` go to `DBL_MAX` at the same point. In that range the true Yoshikawa manipulability ∏σᵢ is still well resolved in double precision, so near-singular configurations become indistinguishable from singular ones. That is exactly where a manipulability threshold gets used.

Reproduction: J = U·diag(3, 2, 1, 0.5, 0.2, σ_min)·Vᵀ with random orthogonal U and V. Measured through the Python bindings (`tesseract-robotics-nanobind` 0.35.0.9):

| σ_min | ∏σ | `m.volume` | min `m.eigen_values` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1e-2 | 6e-3 | 6e-3 | 1e-4 |
| 1e-3 | 6e-4 | 6e-4 | 1e-6 |
| 3e-4 | 1.8e-4 | 0 | 0 |
| 1e-6 | 6e-7 | 0 | 0 |

Forming JJᵀ squares the singular values, so σ = 3e-4 becomes an eigenvalue of 9e-8. That falls below the clipping added in #768, which addressed the negative-eigenvalue NaN from #766, and gets zeroed.

Proposed fix: compute from the SVD of J instead of the eigen-decomposition of JJᵀ (`Eigen::JacobiSVD`). Singular values are non-negative by construction, so the NaN from #766 cannot occur and no clipping is needed. Then volume = ∏σᵢ, eigenvalues = σᵢ², and measure and condition follow from σ_max/σ_min. The force ellipsoid follows from the same decomposition. Happy to open a PR with a unit test that pins volume against ∏σ for a constructed near-singular Jacobian.
new_candidates.title: calcManipulability reports exact singularity for σ_min < ~1e-3 (eigenvalue clipping on JJᵀ)
